name: The Curious Visitor
summary: After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has a troubling discovery about Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man named Maelik visited Thredd with legitimate papers.

sections.title: A Breach in Protocol
sections.body: Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd had not been abandoned by his former comrades, as the guards believed. Months before the riot, a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects the visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He gathers a physical description and sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston to learn who the visitor was.

sections.title: Ties to the Stonemasons
sections.body: Baros Alexston worked closely with Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild before their rebellion. The name Maelik means nothing to him, and the description could fit countless former craftsmen. Yet the visitor had valid clearance to enter the Stockade. That points beyond common criminals slipping past the guards: Defias sympathizers and agents remain deeply embedded in Stormwind's civic offices.

faq.q: Who is the curious visitor mentioned in the quest?
faq.answer: The visitor gave his name as Maelik. For months before the Stockade riot, he visited Bazil Thredd once or twice a week and carried seemingly legitimate identification papers.

faq.q: Why does Warden Thelwater send you to Baros Alexston?
faq.answer: Warden Thelwater sends you to Baros Alexston because he is Stormwind's City Architect and once worked alongside Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild. Since the Defias began among the Stonemasons, Thelwater hopes Alexston may recognize the visitor through his former guild contacts.

faq.q: How did Maelik enter the Stockade without being caught?
faq.answer: Maelik entered the Stockade with legitimate paperwork that cleared prison security checks. The guards had no legal cause to deny him entry, which suggests a bureaucratic error or corrupt officials inside the kingdom's administration.

faq.q: What role did Bazil Thredd play in the prison riots?
faq.answer: Bazil Thredd was an imprisoned leader of the Defias Brotherhood in the Stockade. He organized and led the inmates' violent uprising, likely coordinated through his visits with Maelik.

faq.q: What happens after Baros Alexston reads the description?
faq.answer: Baros Alexston recognizes neither the name Maelik nor Thelwater's description. He agrees to investigate further because the visitor must have connections in the city.

faq.q: Why is the visitor important to the investigation of the Defias?
faq.answer: The regular visits show that the Stockade riot was a planned Defias plot, not a spontaneous outburst of lawless rage. Someone with high-level access to Stormwind's official papers helped make it possible.

angles.text: As a human, you can see how forged or sanctioned entry papers expose deep vulnerabilities and possible corruption within the Kingdom of Stormwind's government.
As an Alliance member, you know finding Bazil Thredd's mysterious contact matters to rooting out Defias sympathizers operating openly in the capital.
As a rogue, you recognize the craft behind passing every prison inspection with proper documentation.
